tasks.subject: Humanities
tasks.commandTermDefinition: Break down in order to bring out the essential elements or structure. (Identify parts and relationships, interpret patterns, and extract meaningful conclusions).
tasks.title: Urban Transit Accessibility vs. Household Income
tasks.prompt: Analyze the relationship between median household income, transit access frequency, and car ownership rates across the four city zones. In your analysis, identify key correlations, note any anomalies, and discuss the broader socio-economic implications.

stimulus.title: Public Transit Frequency vs. Household Socio-Economic Indicators (Metro Region)
stimulus.notes: Context: Zone C accommodates 46% of the city's essential shift-workers who commute into the Urban Core daily.

recommendedStructure: 1. Identification of the primary correlation (transit frequency vs. income / car dependency)
2. Contrast and anomaly analysis (examine Zone C vs. Zone D: forced vs. voluntary car ownership)
3. Analytical conclusion on structural inequality and economic mobility
sentenceStarters: The data demonstrates a distinct correlation between...
A significant divergence is evident when contrasting Zone C and Zone D, as...
This disparity suggests that for lower-income households, car ownership is not an asset but a...
Consequently, the inadequate transit provision in Zone C exacerbates...
wordsToAvoid: I think / In my opinion (Use: 'The data indicates' or 'It is apparent that')
rubricChecklist: Synthesized multiple data columns rather than reciting raw numbers isolated from context
Distinguished between correlation and underlying socio-economic causation
Critically evaluated the disparity between Zone C and Zone D
Maintained objective, evidence-based academic register throughout

tasks.subject: Sciences
tasks.commandTermDefinition: Give valid reasons or evidence to support an answer or conclusion.
tasks.mypCriterion: Criterion C: Processing and Evaluating / Criterion D: Reflecting on Science Impacts
tasks.title: Selection of Groundwater Nitrate Remediation Technology
tasks.prompt: Justify the selection of Method B (Subsurface Permeable Bio-Barriers) over Method A and Method C as the optimal municipal intervention for agricultural runoff contamination, taking into account efficacy, environmental footprint, and municipal constraints.

stimulus.title: Performance and Resource Trial Data: Nitrate Remediation Technologies
stimulus.notes: Constraints: Municipal annual budget cap is $60,000. Land available adjacent to watershed is restricted to 2.0 hectares.

recommendedStructure: 1. Direct stance & thesis: explicit selection of Method B framed by feasibility parameters
2. Multi-criteria justification: balance of high efficiency (89%) with budgetary compliance ($38k vs $60k cap)
3. Systematic refutation: demonstrate why Method A (budgetary overage) and Method C (spatial overage) fail
sentenceStarters: Method B is conclusively the most viable remediation strategy because...
Although Method A achieves a marginally superior removal efficiency of 94%, it is rendered unfeasible by...
Furthermore, Method C violates the spatial constraint of 2.0 hectares, requiring...
By eliminating secondary hazardous byproducts while operating well below the $60,000 threshold, Method B balances...
wordsToAvoid: It is the best (Replace with: 'presents the optimal balance of efficiency and feasibility')
rubricChecklist: Explicitly stated choice in the initial sentence without ambiguity
Directly referenced and compared quantitative metrics across all three methods
Addressed external constraints (budget cap & land availability) as core justification
Refuted competing alternatives using concrete scientific/operational reasoning

tasks.subject: Sciences
tasks.commandTermDefinition: Make an appraisal by weighing up the strengths and limitations.
tasks.mypCriterion: Criterion D: Reflecting on the impacts of science
tasks.title: Industrial Desalination Efficacy in Coastal Ecosystems
tasks.prompt: Evaluate the viability of implementing reverse osmosis versus solar electrodialysis for municipal water purification in a semi-arid coastal municipality.

stimulus.title: Performance, Energetic, and Ecological Metrics of Candidate Desalination Technologies
stimulus.notes: Municipal constraints: The facility must border a protected marine sanctuary with strict regulations capping effluent salinity at 1.5x ambient levels. Grid electricity costs $0.22/kWh; local solar irradiance averages 6.2 kWh/m²/day.

recommendedStructure: 1. Definitive comparative thesis balancing thermal/chemical output against water recovery yields.
2. Synthesis of data: weigh operational efficiency (recovery/energy) against ecological liabilities.
3. Concluding judgment identifying the optimal method under the explicit municipal constraints.
sentenceStarters: While SWRO demonstrates superior volumetric throughput, its ecological footprint is compromised by...
A comparative assessment reveals that Solar-EDR balances energy inputs with...
Despite the established reliability of thermal distillation, MSF remains untenable due to...
Consequently, the data indicates that Solar-EDR represents the most viable solution because...
wordsToAvoid: I think / In my opinion (Use: 'The quantitative data indicates' or 'Comparative appraisal confirms')
bad for fish (Use: 'detrimental to marine benthic organisms')
a lot of power (Use: 'excessive specific energy consumption')
rubricChecklist: Identified strengths and limitations for at least two technologies based strictly on the table.
Integrated quantitative data (e.g., kWh/m³, recovery percentages, salinity ratios) as direct justification.
Addressed the environmental constraints (sanctuary limits, energy costs) to form an unambiguous appraisal.
Maintained a formal academic register without subjective personal pronouns.

tasks.subject: Design
tasks.commandTermDefinition: Give a detailed account including reasons or causes.
tasks.title: Material Suitability for Commuter Meal Containers
tasks.prompt: Explain how material properties and lifecycle metrics determine the suitability of container candidates for active urban cyclists.

stimulus.title: Material Specification Matrix for Secondary Food Storage Containers
stimulus.notes: Target user profile: Commuters travel via bicycle in varied weather. Design specification requires high impact resistance during accidental transit drops, minimal carry-weight, and rapid office reheating capability.

recommendedStructure: 1. Direct statement linking specific material requirements (mass, resilience, reheating) to user needs.
2. Detailed cause-and-effect explanation analyzing why certain materials fail specific operational thresholds.
3. Synthesis explaining the primary candidate's balanced performance across lifecycle and functional metrics.

Although anodized aluminum offers superior yield strength (276 MPa), its utility is eliminated by...
The elevated density of borosilicate glass (2.23 g/cm³) combined with shear brittleness introduces...
Hence, food-grade polypropylene emerges as the most functional solution because its low density...
wordsToAvoid: easy to break (Use: 'susceptible to brittle fracture under dynamic shock')
rubricChecklist: Provided clear causal mechanisms (e.g., density impacting transit fatigue; microwave non-compliance causing functional rejection).
Directly referenced comparative metrics from the stimulus table to substantiate the explanation.
Addressed all three design parameters: weight, durability, and reheating functionality.
Conformed to the 120-150 word limitation while sustaining an analytical tone.
